text:
oncall-bot: Pager: SEV2 - RDMA link flaps + packet loss observed from serving pool -> multiple GPUs reporting CUDA OOMs and container restarts. Root ts: 3369998888

sara-ng: seeing repeated 'RC timeout' and 'QP retry exceeded' messages in /var/log/messages on rack-rdma-07. Containers on node gpu-07-03 restarted twice in last 6m.

kai-chen: tagging in. are we sure it's fabric not software? any driver resets in dmesg?

lee: quick grab: 
```
May 03 12:04:02 gpu-07-03 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: MLX5: Reset request from firmware (reason 0x8)
May 03 12:04:03 gpu-07-03 runtime: cuda: out of memory while allocating 1.2GB
May 03 12:05:10 gpu-07-03 containerd: container restarted (exit code 137)
```

maria-g: customers in us-west-2 seeing elevated 5xxs and latency spikes. support says two downstream accounts (acct-omega and acct-primus) reported errors.

sara-ng: confirmed correlation: packet retransmits on IB counters concurrent with kworker stalls. metrics: if_in_errs and rx_dropped up.

infra-bot: ibport status for rack-rdma-07: port 1 flapping (up/down 4 times in 5m). link speed degraded to SDR.

kai-chen: ok immediate mitigations: 1) cordon node gpu-07-03 from serving group; 2) enable degraded fallback routing to dedicated-region replica pool; 3) throttle heavy batchers to reduce memory pressure. can someone run iperf and ib_read_bw on the host?

lee: running quick checks: 
```
# on gpu-07-03
ibstat mlx5_0
ib_devinfo -d mlx5_0
ibv_rc_pingpong -s 4096 host-peer
```
Results: pingpong shows 20-40% packet loss, latency spikes ~>2000us.

sara-ng: running neighbor probe: suspect switch side — ports 23/24 on leaf-07 show high CRC. opening ticket with colo. tagging @support-ops for customer comms.

support-ops: preparing holding message for affected accounts: "We are investigating a fabric issue causing transient errors and elevated latency for inference. Engineers have applied mitigations and we will provide updates every 15m."

maria-g: sending to acct-omega now. they asked for ETA. we have to be conservative.

kai-chen: temporary config applied: set routing policy to prefer us-west-2-fallback (non-shared pool) for traffic hitting model gpt-large. Applied automatic fallback to quantized variant gpt-large-q.

sara-ng: also forcing smaller batch sizes on affected nodes: set BATCHER_MAX_TOKENS=512 and BATCHER_MAX_CONCURRENCY=8 for pool gpu-07.

lee: started full driver logs capture and collected coredump from container; uploading to /tmp/incident-dumps/3369998888.tar.gz

infra-bot: note: mlx5 driver firmware mismatch detected on gpu-07-03 (fw 27.0.1 vs cluster standard 28.1.0). nonblocking but increases reset risk.

kai-chen: that aligns with flapping. ask colo to move that server off the fabric or reboot switch port. Sara, can you coordinate with colo ops?

sara-ng: on it. raised ticket COL0-1149: switch leaf-07 port 23/24 diag + force reset. colo responded initial ack, ETA 18m.

maria-g: customers want priority. proposing to promote dedicated-reserved pool for their traffic while we triage. Support asks for exact list of affected request IDs, can we extract?

lee: yes pulling traces now, will attach errors and top-k stacks. I can also run a live migrate of hot models off gpu-07-0x nodes.

kai-chen: next steps for oncall: 1) maintain throttles and fallback; 2) cordon problematic nodes; 3) if colo can't stabilize, failover entire rack to standby region; 4) gather driver/firmware evidence for postmortem.

sara-ng: handing off to @kai-chen for next shift at 12:30 UTC. I will remain on call for colo coordination for 18m.

oncall-bot: Handoff acknowledged. New oncall: kai-chen. Pager escalations will route to kai-chen.

support-ops: update posted to impacted accounts. they accepted fallback plan for acct-omega and asked for daily updates until fixed.

kai-chen: I've started a rolling fallback job: 
```
# trigger fallback route
redwood route apply --pool us-west-2-fallback --selector rack:rack-rdma-07 --grace 60s
```
Monitoring token-level latencies.

lee: after cordon and fallback, OOMs dropped by ~85% on other nodes but gpu-07-03 still showing kernel resets. container restart rate reduced from 4/min to 1/hour cluster-wide.

sara-ng: colo updated: they replaced SFP on leaf-07 and cleared CRC errors. monitoring says no further flaps in last 4m.

maria-g: CS reached out — they've seen 90% reduction in errors for acct-omega. they're requesting a postmortem and ETA for full restoration.

kai-chen: plan: keep fallback until cluster nodes with mismatched firmware are reprovisioned. schedule maintenance window to upgrade fw on affected hosts. I'll file infra ticket to upgrade to 28.1.0 and blacklist older images.

sara-ng: agreed. immediate: mark incident as mitigated, but keep incident channel open for 2h monitoring. I'll draft notes for postmortem.

oncall-bot: Incident status set -> MITIGATED (partial). Next update due in 15m.

maria-g: thanks team. Support will send final customer note after 15m confirmation.

kai-chen: handoff complete. leaving detailed TODOs in the incident doc and will coordinate fw upgrades.

support-ops: please add timeline and customer impact to the incident doc: number of affected requests, impacted accounts, duration, and mitigation steps.

sara-ng: will add. attaching logs and ib counters to ticket COL0-1149 and infra ticket INF-3372.

lee: saving trace bundle to s3://redwood-incident-logs/3369998888/ for postmortem.

oncall-bot: Thread archived for followups.
